result:
**Answer: c = 1/25**, obtained from a lower-bound construction. I did not verify a matching upper bound, so this is a best estimate rather than a proven value.

**Construction.** Take a blow-up of the 5-cycle C₅ with parts V₁,…,V₅ of size n/5. Join V_i completely to V_{i±1}. Inside each part, place a sparse triangle-free graph with independence number o(n), such as an Erdős-type graph.

- **K₅-free:** C₅ has no triangles, so a clique uses at most 2 vertices from any part (since each part is triangle-free internally). A clique can therefore span at most two adjacent parts, giving at most 2 + 2 = 4 vertices.
- **α(G) = o(n):** Any independent set is built from independent sets inside parts, and two parts can be combined only when they are non-adjacent. Each such contribution is o(n).
- **Cost of bipartization:** The internal edges total o(n²), so they are negligible. The dense edges form a C₅ blow-up. A bipartition of C₅ must leave one pair of adjacent parts on the same side, and that pair contributes (n/5)² = n²/25 monochromatic edges. A fractional split of parts does not do better for uniform weights, so the minimum number of edges to delete is n²/25 + o(n²).

This gives c ≥ 1/25.

**Caveat.** I did not establish that uniform weights on C₅ are optimal over all triangle-free reduced graphs with weights, nor that the general upper bound matches. I also did not check the literature on this problem.

ANSWER: 1/25
